questions.question: When should data-dependent imputation and scaling statistics be fitted?
options: On the training partition only
On the validation and test partitions together
On every row before the split
Only after production scoring
questions.explanation: Learning transformation state from evaluation rows leaks information into the model-development process.

questions.question: What does merge(validate="many_to_one") protect?
options: It checks that each left row matches at most one right-side key
It converts every key to a string
It removes unmatched rows automatically
It sorts both inputs by time
questions.explanation: The cardinality contract catches duplicate dimension keys that could multiply training examples.

questions.question: Why should nullable join keys be handled explicitly before a pandas merge?
options: pandas can match null keys to each other, unlike usual SQL semantics
pandas always drops rows with null keys
Null keys disable vectorized execution
Null keys force a many-to-many validation mode
questions.explanation: pandas warns that null keys may match one another, so production joins should define and test the intended behavior.

questions.question: What is wrong with a rolling feature that includes observations after prediction time?
options: It leaks evidence unavailable when the prediction is made
It uses too little memory
It cannot produce numeric output
It always changes the row count
questions.explanation: Time-dependent features must stop at the prediction boundary and be evaluated with forward-moving splits.

questions.question: Which action should usually come before adding parallel workers to a pandas job?
options: Profile, project columns, filter rows, and improve dtypes
Convert fixed-width columns to Python objects
Concatenate one row at a time
Copy the full DataFrame to every worker
questions.explanation: Reducing materialized data and temporary work is often simpler and more effective than paying process serialization and copying costs.

questions.question: When is chunking a valid memory-control strategy?
options: When each chunk needs little or explicitly managed cross-chunk state
Whenever a global sort is required
Only when all chunks remain in memory
Whenever model fitting requires every row simultaneously
questions.explanation: Chunking bounds peak memory only when the computation can be reduced incrementally or its shared state is controlled.

questions.question: Why must a production pipeline pin and test its pandas version?
options: Dtypes, Copy-on-Write behavior, and operation semantics can vary across versions
A version pin automatically prevents data leakage
Only pinned versions support DataFrames
A version pin replaces output-schema tests
questions.explanation: Reproducibility requires an explicit environment plus schema and parity tests; version-sensitive behavior cannot be assumed.

questions.question: What is the strongest evidence that offline and serving features agree?
options: Shared fixtures compare ordered columns, dtypes, null handling, and values
Both paths use similarly named functions
The training job finishes without warnings
The DataFrame has the expected number of rows
questions.explanation: Parity tests should compare the actual feature contract and representative values, including edge cases.
